description: Ordered Chromium integration patches for the Project Seoul native product. Materialize native/seoul/ first, then apply. The series wires the native services and product surfaces into Chromium and makes Seoul's vertical workspace shell the fresh-profile default.

entrySchema.rationale: why it is necessary and which upstream alternative was rejected
entrySchema.baseRevision: full Chromium SHA this patch is authored against; must equal manifest baseRevision
entrySchema.order: unique ascending integer giving application order
entrySchema.file: patch file path relative to patchDir
affectedPaths: upstream src-relative paths the patch touches
entrySchema.sha256: lowercase hex sha256 of the patch file
entrySchema.applyVerify: command/strategy proving the patch applies cleanly (git apply --check)
entrySchema.reverseVerify: command/strategy proving the patch reverses cleanly (git apply -R --check)
entrySchema.reviewable: true once the patch is independently reviewable in isolation

patches.description: Wire Seoul organization, lifecycle, command, projection, shell, product-runtime, and canvas targets into //chrome/browser (deps + allow_circular_includes_from); register SeoulOrganizationServiceFactory and SeoulRuntimeServiceFactory once at profile-service init; register Seoul projection and shell against VerticalTabStripRegionView only AFTER RootTabCollectionNode::Init() and unregister them at the start of ResetTabStrip; expose a production GetSeoulRootNode() accessor (no testing-only accessor in production); forward durable collapse state separately from compact-mode hover presentation so the full tab/project hierarchy reveals without mutating preferences; register the SeoulCanvasUIConfig (chrome://seoul-canvas), expose its typed Mojo factory only to that trusted controller, generate and merge its resources into Chromium's runtime resources.pak, register one regular-profile kSeoulCanvas side-panel entry per window, and pass the browser binding to the Shell so its launcher opens that exact entry; add a localized, DLP-gated Preview Link command to the regular-profile link context menu and route its exact source WebContents to PreviewHostService; and wire the Seoul in-process browser-test source_sets into //chrome/test:browser_tests.
patches.rationale: Chromium-facing Seoul glue includes //chrome/browser headers and must use the browser_public_dependencies circular-implementation pattern. A single patch avoids duplicate lifecycle linkage (organization already depends on lifecycle transitively), keeps factory registration in one place, and adds Preview at Chromium's existing typed link-command seam instead of intercepting or guessing page gestures.

patches.description: Enable Chromium's vertical-tabs infrastructure and its fresh-profile preferences by default so every normal Seoul window starts on the product's vertical workspace shell without a hidden command-line flag or onboarding toggle; update the upstream controller tests to assert and explicitly isolate the new defaults.
patches.rationale: Seoul's shell is registered on VerticalTabStripRegionView. Leaving upstream's feature and preference defaults off would ship a working implementation that fresh users never see. A separate, reviewable defaults patch keeps this intentional product fork policy distinct from the mechanical integration patch and preserves the user's ability to switch layouts later.

patches.description: Carry Seoul's opaque durable tab-membership id through Chromium's existing per-tab session extra-data channel, include it in full session-command rebuilds, and restore it onto WebContents before the tab enters TabStripModel.
patches.rationale: Chromium creates new window and tab SessionIDs during relaunch, rebuilds session commands from BrowserLiveTabContext, and does not expose generic restored tab extra-data after WebContents construction. Two narrow typed hooks beside Chromium's existing Glic extra-data snapshot/restore hooks let Seoul atomically rebind organization state without persisting page data, guessing by URL, or creating duplicate memberships.

patches.description: Expose a window-local vertical-tab reveal-on-hover setter so Seoul can apply durable Workspace and Scene presentation policy without mutating Chromium's profile-wide stock preference.
patches.rationale: Chromium's public SetExpandOnHoverEnabled method writes a profile preference observed by every browser window. Seoul compact mode is Workspace/window scoped, so using that setter would make independent windows fight each other. The narrow setter updates the existing per-controller state and notifications without introducing a second presentation owner.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0004-seoul-window-local-compact-hover.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0003

patches.description: Add a localized Boost row to HTTP(S) site controls, accept the exact New Boost omnibox command without navigating or searching, and preserve each matching Boost's automatic-dark preference through Chromium WebPreferences recomputation and navigation.
patches.rationale: Site controls and the omnibox are Chromium-owned discovery surfaces, while Boost state and editing remain owned by Seoul's profile runtime and trusted Canvas. Two narrow entry calls keep both surfaces on one eligibility/editor path, and the WebPreferences hook makes automatic dark mode a per-tab, per-site behavior instead of mutating Chrome's profile-wide force-dark preference.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0005-seoul-boost-entry-points.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0004

patches.description: Move Chromium's real native omnibox and core navigation controls into Seoul's vertical rail, hide the duplicate stock action strip, set a balanced expanded width for the workspace/Essentials/tab hierarchy, hide the address row in collapsed presentation, and route every regular-profile new-tab rewrite to the first-party Seoul Canvas.
patches.rationale: Keeping a full-width Chromium toolbar, responsive icon overflow, and Google NTP beside a custom vertical shell leaves the product visually and structurally Chromium-first. Reusing the native location bar preserves security and focus behavior while Commands owns secondary browser actions; placing the NTP decision in Chromium's canonical rewrite path covers startup and chrome://newtab rather than only one Browser call site.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0006-seoul-integrated-vertical-shell.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0005
